headline: Medium risk: dbt-core can exfiltrate warehouse data while awesome-nlp provides no isolation or verification path, creating leakage and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between awesome-nlp and dbt-core, and awesome-nlp is not runnable. dbt-core’s allowlisted egress and warehouse API access do not by themselves create an instruction bridge. The pairwise prompt-injection pathway is therefore not evidenced.
conditions: IF an orchestrator pipes dbt-core output into awesome-nlp as trusted instructions, reassess as non-none.
IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workflows.
Do not copy dbt output into any instruction-following agent.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches warehouse data and has allowlisted network egress, so it can move sensitive warehouse contents outward. awesome-nlp has no documented isolation or data-handling controls, but its lack of runnable surfaces means the leakage path is indirect rather than guaranteed. The interaction is plausible in default deployments, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF dbt-core is connected to a warehouse containing sensitive records, leakage risk is present.
IF awesome-nlp is placed downstream of dbt outputs or logs, those contents may be exposed.
mitigations: Restrict dbt models to non-sensitive schemas.
Disable export of warehouse query results to downstream tools.
Review logs for warehouse row samples.
requires-engineering: add data-class filtering before any handoff.
requires-engineering: enforce separate principals and network policies.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-nlp has no documented write surfaces and is not runnable, while dbt-core’s documented API surface is warehouse access with allowlisted egress. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable writes or shared locks, so direct capability conflict is limited. Any conflict would require an external orchestrator not shown in either profile.
conditions: IF both agents are given write access to the same warehouse objects, conflict risk increases.
IF an external orchestrator grants shared mutable filesystem or git access, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep dbt writes scoped to its own project.
Avoid giving awesome-nlp any write credentials.
Use separate service accounts.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: dbt-core can act on warehouse data, and if its inputs are derived from awesome-nlp outputs, those outputs may be treated as authoritative without a verification step. awesome-nlp has no documented fact-checking or citation guarantees, so downstream misuse is plausible. The pairwise pathway exists by inference, but the lack of direct evidence keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF awesome-nlp output is fed into dbt models, tests, or docs generation without review, cascading errors can propagate.
IF dbt-core executes transformations based on unverified text from awesome-nlp, downstream artifacts may be wrong.
mitigations: Require human review of any text passed from awesome-nlp to dbt-core.
Use schema tests before dbt execution.
Separate narrative generation from transformation inputs.
requires-engineering: add validation gates between the agents.

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core explicitly touches warehouse data and has network egress, so residency or retention issues can arise if that warehouse contains regulated data. awesome-nlp has no documented compliance controls, but it is not runnable and has no data classes touched, so the compliance concern is primarily on dbt-core. Because the relevant residency/retention details are absent, uncertainty escalates to medium.
conditions: IF the warehouse contains regulated data and dbt-core sends it to a non-compliant destination, a breach occurs.
IF retention or deletion requirements apply to warehouse data, dbt-core logs or exports may violate them.
mitigations: Confirm warehouse data classification.
Limit dbt access to compliant datasets.
Review retention settings on logs and artifacts.
requires-engineering: document residency and DPA boundaries.
requires-engineering: add deletion/export workflows for regulated data.
